subject: SIG addendum: Offline update & artifact transfer process for on-prem deployments
messages:
From: Terry Hughes <terry.hughes@hillside.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hillside.com
Date: 2026-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem SIG addendum: offline updates & delivery

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement we need a brief SIG-style addendum covering how Redwood handles offline updates and artifact delivery for on-prem / air-gapped deployments. Specifically we want clarity on:

- How updates are provided to air-gapped systems (media, signed artifacts, or pull by customer)
- Integrity verification (signatures, checksums) and signing authority
- Support model for applying updates (remote assist, on-site, runbook)
- Evidence/artifact we can attach to our internal SIG/Procurement package

Can you share a short addendum and any sample artifacts? Procurement would like a viewable PDF and a machine-readable manifest if possible.

Best,
Terry Hughes
Director of Infrastructure, Hillside Systems
[terry.hughes@hillside.com]

[Attachment: requirements_summary.pdf (PDF, 76 KB)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Terry Hughes <terry.hughes@hillside.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem SIG addendum: offline updates & delivery

Terry —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a draft SIG addendum that lays out our offline update process, artifact delivery options, and the support model for air-gapped installs. Quick highlights:

- Delivery options: encrypted USB shipment (customer or vendor-managed), signed tarball via SFTP transfer to a customer-controlled ingress node, or physical media shipping.
- Integrity: artifacts are signed with a Redwood release key; SHA256 manifest provided; optional PGP signatures for customer pre-shared keys.
- Support: we offer remote guided installs (customer pushes artifacts), on-site subcontractor support for urgent upgrades (SOW), and detailed runbooks for customer operations teams.
- Evidence: we can provide a PDF addendum, a machine-readable CSV manifest, and a checksum signature file for each release.

I attached the draft addendum and an SFTP instruction stub. Dev / Marcus — could you confirm the manifest columns and whether we should include an HSM signing note?

Attachments: [SIG_Addendum_v1.0.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)], [SFTP_Instructions.txt (TXT, 3 KB)]

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem SIG addendum: offline updates & delivery

Rachel / Marcus / Terry —

Reviewed the draft. A few technical clarifications and a suggested manifest schema:

- Manifest CSV columns we recommend: filename, relative_path, size_bytes, sha256_hex, release_version, signed_by_key_id, signature_filename
- Signing: artifacts are signed using our release HSM-managed RSA key. We can provide detached signatures (.sig) and the public key fingerprint. For customers that require PGP we can also provide a PGP-signed manifest using a customer-supplied PGP key (process documented).
- Transfer: SFTP to a customer ingress host is our preferred secure flow for recurring updates; for one-off air-gap deliveries we produce a signed tarball and ship encrypted media.
- Support windows: Standard support (M-F 9-5 PT) for guided installs; accelerated incident/upgrade assistance available under managed SOWs with 24x7 option.

Attached: artifact_manifest.csv (example with three artifacts)

Notes: Marcus — are we comfortable stating ‘HSM-backed signing’ in the addendum text? If so I'll add a short implementation footnote.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

Thanks for the draft. A couple of procurement/audit items before we finalize:

1) Chain of custody: can you provide a sample manifest with fields indicating originator and timestamp (we use this to feed our internal CAIQ mapping).
2) Evidence packaging: procurement wants the addendum as a signed PDF and a separate machine-readable manifest (CSV) plus a checksum file.
3) DocuSign: Hillside procurement asked for a DocuSign-friendly addendum so they can attach it to the purchase order.

Would you be able to:
- Produce a finalized PDF with an explicit signature block for a Redwood security approver
- Upload the CSV manifest and checksum files to a shared location or provide an SFTP pattern?
